a: A vector space is a set closed under vector addition and scalar multiplication with standard axioms.
Vectors are linearly independent if none is a linear combination of the others.
A basis is a linearly independent set that spans the space.
Rank is the dimension of the column space (number of independent columns/rows).
A⁻¹ exists if det(A) ≠ 0 and A A⁻¹ = I.
E[X] is the long-run average value of random variable X.
Var(X) = E[(X - μ)²] measures spread around the mean.
The normal (Gaussian) distribution is the classic bell curve, parameterized by mean and variance.
Sums of many independent random variables tend toward a normal distribution.
P(A|B) = P(A and B) / P(B) for P(B) > 0
Events A and B are independent if P(A and B) = P(A)P(B).
P(n,k) = n! / (n-k)! ordered selections without replacement.
C(n,k) = n! / (k!(n-k)!) unordered selections without replacement.
Sample averages converge to the expected value as sample size grows.
